newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas urges armed struggle on peace anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Hamas urges armed struggle on peace anniversary.

text.p: The Moslem militant Hamas movement urged Arabs and Moslems on Monday to return to armed struggle against Israel, saying Yasser Arafat's "oppressive regime" and peace deals had failed to regain Palestinian rights.

"We in the Hamas movement...are more convinced of the need to join Palestinian, Arab and Moslem forces together to adopt a comprehensive confrontation programme against the Zionist occupation spearheaded by popular armed resistance," Hamas said in a statement.

The statement was issued to mark the third anniversary of the signing of the September 1993 PLO-Israel peace deal secretly negotiated and signed in Oslo, Norway, which gave Palestinians self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Palestinian President Arafat cracked down on Hamas for carrying out a series of suicide attacks against Israel in February and March that killed 59 people.

Hamas officials said Arafat's security forces jailed more than 900 Hamas and Islamic Jihad activists and damaged their infrastructure by raiding and closing their financial, religious, social and political institutions.
"Any talk on a new reality being built in self-ruled areas is no more than illusions and deceit to cover up for the failure of the...oppressive Authority regime," the statement said.
Hamas opposes the PLO-Israel peace deals and has vowed to wreck them through attacks against the Jewish state.

"We in the Hamas movement believe that partial agreements have failed even in securing the minimum of promises made...The land that Arafat and his collapsing team have claimed they signed Oslo to preserve is slipping through the people's fingers piece by piece," Hamas said.
